pages.title: Start here: how this workspace runs

text.text: This workspace keeps every child on the well-visit and vaccine schedule, and keeps the vaccine fridge honest. It is built around how a pediatric office actually works: visits, the child's chart, each dose, and each lot.
The four tables
Visits

: well-child checks, sick visits, shot-only appointments and sports physicals. Status runs Scheduled, Confirmed, Checked in, Completed. Check in and Mark completed are buttons on each row; Mark completed stamps the day. Screenings done records which age-based screens were given.
Children
: one row per child, first name and last initial only, with guardian, coverage and the next well visit due. Each child shows visits completed, visits booked, doses given and doses still due.
Immunizations
: one row per dose. A dose is Due, Overdue, Scheduled, Deferred, Given or Declined. Mark given stamps the day; two boxes record the information sheet and the state registry report.
Vaccine stock
: every lot, state-supplied or private, with lot number, expiry, doses on hand and a par level.
A normal day
7:45: the lead nurse reads the fridge temperature and checks the Fridge check list on the Dashboard.
Front desk opens Visits, This week view, and confirms tomorrow's families by text.
Before each well visit, the nurse opens the child and looks at Doses due or overdue. Every shot due is given today unless the parent declines; write the reason.
After each dose, choose the lot used. The lot's Doses given count is your audit trail.
At close, the nurse works the Doses to chase list and books catch-up visits.
Who owns what
Two rules that keep you out of trouble
State-supplied doses go only to eligible children. Keep them on their own shelf and their own lot rows.
A declined dose is recorded, never deleted. The parent's reason and the date matter at the next visit.

text.text: A well-child visit is a checklist that changes with age. This page is the order of work the team follows so nothing age-specific is missed and the family leaves with the next visit booked.
What each age needs (our house list)

cells.text: DTaP, IPV, Hib, PCV, rotavirus, hepatitis B
Autism screen at 18 months, lead and hemoglobin at 12

text.text: Check your state's and the national schedule each year; this table is a starting point.
Order of work
Front desk confirms coverage and hands the age's screening form at check-in. Press Check in.
Nurse rooms the child, takes growth, and opens the child's row to see Doses due or overdue.
Provider reviews the screen, examines, and talks through shots with the parent.
Nurse gives the doses, chooses the lot used on each, and ticks Info sheet given.
Provider presses Mark completed and ticks the Screenings done.
Front desk books the next well visit before the family leaves and sets Next well visit due.
When a parent hesitates
"These are the shots due at this age. Which questions can I answer for you?"

Listen first. Most hesitation is about one specific worry, such as fever afterwards or too many shots in one day, and it is answered better by the provider than by a handout. If they choose to wait, mark the dose Deferred with a date to revisit, or Declined with their reason. Never leave it blank.
Close-out checklist
Every dose given today is reported to the state registry
Forms for school or sports signed and scanned
Next visit booked or a reminder set
Balance due checked against what the family paid at the desk

Vaccines are the most expensive thing in the building and the easiest to waste. This page covers the fridge routine, the separate state-supplied stock, and the weekly calls that bring behind children back.
Fridge routine
Read and write the minimum and maximum temperature at open and close. Fridge 2 to 8 C, freezer minus 50 to minus 15 C.
Out of range: do not use the doses. Mark the lots, call the state program or the maker, and wait for an answer before using them.
Oldest expiry at the front. Lots expiring within 60 days get that status so they are used first.
Two kinds of stock

cells.text: Children on Medicaid or CHIP, uninsured or under-insured
Never borrowed for a privately insured child; counted monthly for the program
Cost per dose drives Stock value; order to par weekly

text.text: Ordering
Every Monday the practice manager opens Vaccine stock and looks at Order check.
Private lots marked Order are reordered to twice the par level.
State-supplied lots are requested on the program's own form; enter the new lot on arrival.
Expired lots go to Expired, return and are sent back, never thrown away.
Catch-up calls (Thursday afternoon)
Open Immunizations and the Overdue view.
Call the guardian, offer a nurse-only shot visit (ten minutes, no exam).
Book it from the child's row with Book a visit, and move the dose to Scheduled.
After three tries over a month, send a letter and note it in the dose's page.
Worked example

Amira H. missed her flu shot and is behind on MMR. The nurse books a vaccine-only visit, uses state-supplied MMR because Amira is on CHIP, and gives the flu shot from private stock only because the state flu lot ran out, noting the swap for the monthly count.
